newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam rice market static, export business thin.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam rice market static, export business thin.

text.p: Vietnam's rice export prices have barely moved during the past week due to a lack of buying interest, traders said on Thursday.
"It's really quiet now," said one trader. "Exporters and merchants have been keeping prices down in the hope of getting some business, but there's no buying to speak of."
He said many buyers were taking rice from Pakistan, a cheaper market, and noted there were just eight vessels loading at Saigon Port. Two of the vessels were bound for Iraq, he said.
Traders quoted five-percent broken normal grade rice, FOB Saigon Port, at $280-290 per tonne, barely changed from a week ago. Ten-percent broken was unchanged at $275-280 a tonne.

They said paddy from the main producing area, the Mekong Delta, may still be held up by transport problems caused by flooding. However, there was little concern about supply, especially given the current low level of interest from buyers.
The government last month raised this years's export quota for rice to three million tonnes from 2.5 million.
Vietnam sold 2.025 million tonnes of rice to overseas buyers in 1995, making it the world's fourth-largest exporter of the grain after the United States, Thailand and India.
